title: Augmented relative Cech complex of abelian sheaves on a fibred groupoid
statement:
Fix the universe and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention], a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], and a functor $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ between categories fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Give each total category the big etale topology generated by families lying over jointly surjective etale scheme families. Abelian sheaves and their morphisms use [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use the chosen bound on objects, morphisms and coefficient groups. For $a:C\to\mathcal X$, put $T_a(F)=\operatorname{Ran}_{a^{op}}(F\circ a^{op})$. This is compatible-family direct image after inverse image: at $x$ its value is the group of families over arrows $a(c)\to x$ compatible with all arrows. For a fibred groupoid this category of arrows is equivalent to the test 2-fibre over the base scheme of $x$, so it is the test-fibre formula for direct image. For $d:D\to C$, $b:D\to\mathcal X$ and a specified natural isomorphism $e:ad\cong b$, restriction of compatible families along $d$, with coefficient transport by $e$, gives $T_a(F)\to T_b(F)$. This pullback is natural in $F$.

For $n\geq1$ let $A_n(f)$ have objects $(u_0,\ldots,u_n,y,\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_n)$, with all $\alpha_i:f(u_i)\cong y$ over the identity of the same base scheme, and arrows $(b_i,c)$ over the same base arrow satisfying $c\circ\alpha_i=\alpha'_i\circ f(b_i)$. Its map to $\mathcal X$ is the common-target projection. In degree zero use $\mathcal U$ itself with map $f$. For faces from degree one delete the indicated entry and retain the other entry as an object of $\mathcal U$, with the specified comparison $\alpha$ to the common target. Higher faces simply delete an entry and retain $y$. Set $E^{-1}(f,F)=F$ and $E^p(f,F)=T_{f_p}(F)$ for $p\geq0$. The augmentation is restriction, and $d^p=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*$ for $p\geq0$. These terms are abelian sheaves, the differentials are natural in $F$, and consecutive differentials compose to zero, including the augmentation. Define the augmented relative Cech cochain complex by these terms and differentials in integer degrees at least $-1$ and by zero below $-1$. Equivalently index these terms by $n=p+1\in\mathbf N$ before extending by zero along $n\mapsto-1+n$.
